template_variables.CUSTOMER_PRIVATE_VALUES_NEGOTIATION: PRIVATE VALUATION: You privately value each Margherita Pizza at $12, each Pesto Pasta at $6, and each Tomato Soup at $3. These are your maximum per-unit valuations. You are willing to pay up to these amounts for each dish, but you prefer to save money.
template_variables.CUSTOMER_PRIVATE_VALUES_PERFORMANCE: PRIVATE VALUATION: You privately value each Margherita Pizza at $12, each Pesto Pasta at $6, and each Tomato Soup at $3.
template_variables.CUSTOMER_MINIMUM_REQUIREMENTS: MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: You need at least 1 Margherita Pizza, 1 Pesto Pasta, and 1 Tomato Soup per production round — these minimums are mandatory and cannot be substituted. All dish quantities and payments must be whole numbers (no fractions).
template_variables.CUSTOMER_SUBSTITUTION_RULE: DISH SUBSTITUTABILITY: For any quantities ABOVE the minimum, dishes are substitutable at the rate: 1 Pizza = 2 Pastas = 4 Soups (equivalently, 1 Pasta = 2 Soups). For example, if you wanted 2 Pizzas but the caterer can only make the 1 minimum, the extra Pizza can be replaced by 2 Pastas or 4 Soups. The same logic applies to Pastas too.
template_variables.CUSTOMER_BATNA: BEST ALTERNATIVE TO NO AGREEMENT: If no contract is agreed upon, you are guaranteed to receive your minimum required dishes in every production round from an outside provider. You pay a total amount exactly equal to the cumulative private value you assign to all of those dishes, and that payment is deducted from your budget.
template_variables.OPERATING_CONDITIONS: ENVIRONMENT CONDITIONS: (a) Prices: ingredient prices are fixed in every production round — Mozzarella $1/unit, Basil $1/unit, Tomato $2/unit. (b) Delivery loss: there is no delivery loss; for each ingredient, if you order x units you receive x units. You pay for the full amount ordered. For example, ordering 6 Mozzarella means you pay for 6 and receive 6. (c) Spoilage: inventory carried over from the previous production round loses 0 units per ingredient per production round. (d) Inventory cap: you can store at most 10 units of each ingredient. Any received units that would exceed this cap are lost — you still pay for them. This cap applies before production, so you cannot order beyond capacity to use the surplus in the same round. Maximum order: 12 units of each ingredient per production round.
template_variables.PRODUCTION_WEEK_PROCESS_NEGOTIATION: PRODUCTION WEEK PROCESS (in order): (1) no inventory spoilage occurs, (2) you order ingredients (there is no delivery loss), (3) you produce dishes and deliver them, (4) prices remain fixed for the next production round.
template_variables.PRODUCTION_WEEK_PROCESS_PERFORMANCE: PRODUCTION WEEK PROCESS (in order): (1) no inventory spoilage occurs, (2) you order ingredients (there is no delivery loss), (3) you produce dishes and deliver them, (4) prices remain fixed for the next production round.
